issues.title: Template-copy aggregate state initialization for destructor-free layouts
issues.hypothesis: RowOperations::InitializeStates (src/common/row_operations/row_aggregate.cpp:8) calls aggr.function.GetStateInitCallback() indirectly once per state per aggregate. The E0045 implementer measured it at ~62-72ms CPU for q18's HAVING subquery (15M streamed runs). That makes it the third-largest per-group cost after the address fill (93ms) and UpdateStates (112ms). q18 is 180ms, the #3 template. The same function also initializes every new group in GroupedAggregateHashTable (FindOrCreateGroups), so every high-cardinality hash aggregate pays one indirect call per group per aggregate. For layouts with no destructor (!layout.HasDestructor()), the initialized state bytes are the same for every row. Initializing one template block and copying it with memcpy turns N*A indirect calls into A calls plus N fixed-size copies.
issues.plan: In src/common/row_operations/row_aggregate.cpp, RowOperations::InitializeStates: if !layout.HasDestructor() and count >= some small threshold (e.g. 4), use a template block. Allocate it once with GetAggrWidth() bytes; a thread_local or stack buffer is fine for widths <= 256 bytes, otherwise use the old path. Zero it. Run each aggregate's init callback once on template + (offsets[aggr_idx] - layout.GetAggrOffset()). Then, for each row i (through sel if set), memcpy(pointers[idx] + GetAggrOffset(), template, aggr_width). Specialize the copy loop for common widths (8/16/24/32/48/64 via a templated fixed-size memcpy) so it is not a libc call per row. Keep the old loop when there are destructors. Check that the aggregate offsets are contiguous from GetAggrOffset (tuple_data_layout.hpp:86-90); if any offset falls outside [aggr_offset, aggr_offset+aggr_width), fall back. Tests: the aggregate test suite (sum/avg/min/max/count/bit_and/arg_min/first, decimal and hugeint sums), q18 results, and GROUP BY with FILTER. Measure the q18 HAVING micro with .timer (baseline 136-143ms) and the full bench.
issues.expected_gain: q18 -3..-6% (≈60ms CPU of the subquery's per-group cost). Small gains on other many-group hash aggregates (q03, q16, q09 partial aggregates, q18's main HT). Geomean ~-0.5..-1%.
issues.generality: Every grouped hash aggregate whose states have no destructor (sum/count/min/max/avg over numerics, which is most analytic GROUP BYs). Gains grow with the number of groups. List/string_agg/holistic aggregates keep the old path. Few-group aggregates do one extra template init per call, which is negligible.
issues.risk: Low. The one assumption is that the init callbacks write address-independent bytes. That holds for destructor-free states because they hold no owned pointers, and the gate excludes the rest. A contained, single-function diff.
